_provenance.note: tgId 49, tcId 343 (curve P-521, hashAlg SHA2-512) — the group's sole testPassed=true case among its 7 (the other 6 are deliberate negative cases: zero r, modify message, modify s, modify r, modify key, zero s). qx/qy/r/s are each exactly 66 bytes (canonical P-521 field/order width — ceil(521/8)), matching OSSLECDSA::verify's `signature.size() != 2 * orderLen` check, with no leading-zero stripping required. Independently re-verified against Python's cryptography library (49.0.0) before use: EllipticCurvePublicNumbers(qx, qy, SECP521R1()).public_key().verify(encode_dss_signature(r, s), message_bytes, ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA512())) raised no exception — VALID, matching ACVP's own testPassed=true label. REPLACES a file that carried no _provenance block and no real source at all: its first test case's `msg` was the literal placeholder ASCII string "ACVP ECDSA P-521 SigVer test vector" and its second case's `msg` was a hex encoding of the literal English sentence "ECDSA P-521 extra test vector for sigVer differentiation" — both fabricated, not drawn from any standard or real ACVP pull, i.e. Tier-4-and-below (self-generated) material that the remediation plan's §1 ladder never accepts as sole evidence. Same source file and same source_sha256 as ecdsa_test.json (P-256) and ecdsa_p384_test.json (P-384) — ECDSA-SigVer-1.0/internalProjection.json covers all NIST-standard prime curves in one document. UNLIKE the P-256/P-384 files, this vector is NOT wired into tests/acvp-wasm.mjs — no ECDSA P-521 block exists there at all today, for a genuine, verified reason: tests/helpers.mjs's importECPublicKey() builds the CKA_EC_POINT DER OCTET STRING with a single raw length byte (`derPoint[1] = pointLen`), which is only valid BER/DER short-form encoding for pointLen < 128. P-521's uncompressed point is 1 + 66 + 66 = 133 bytes, so that helper cannot construct a valid EC_POINT for P-521 as written (133 = 0x85 would be misread as a long-form length-of-length prefix, not a length). Fixing that generically (long-form DER length encoding) plus adding a P-521 SigVer block and confirming CKM_ECDSA_SHA512 dispatch end-to-end through the WASM ABI is a real, separate piece of work, left for a follow-up rather than done as a side effect of this provenance fix. src/lib/crypto/OSSLECDSA.cpp itself has no P-521-specific restriction — getMaxKeySize() explicitly returns 521 ("Biggest EC group is secp521r1") and CKM_ECDSA_SHA512 is dispatched identically to the other hash-then-verify mechanisms via EVP_DigestVerify — so the constraint here is in the test harness's point encoding, not the engine.
